outflow cap (issue #37): the conservative cascade computed every alpha/beta flow from pre-step heat and subtracted it from the decayed value (heat*decay), then clamped the result at 0 in the commit step. A node with an in-link sends alpha*heat in total and a node with an out-link sends beta*heat, so whenever alpha+beta exceeded decay the node was overdrawn, the clamp discarded the negative balance, and the flows it had already delivered became new heat (real page, router.ts seeded with 5, alpha=beta=1, decay=0.5: total 5 -> 10 -> 15 -> 30 -> 43.1 -> 86.3 -> 123.0 in 6 steps; 6190 of 9702 swept slider settings created heat). Fixed in the Step Convolution handler: step 1 now also computes a per-node outScale = decay / (alpha[if inDegree>0] + beta[if outDegree>0]) when that sum exceeds decay, else exactly 1, and both flow expressions are multiplied by outScale of their origin node. Total outflow can therefore never exceed the node's decayed heat, the clamp never fires on a negative balance, and total heat after a step is exactly decay * total before (0 of 9702 settings create heat; worst per-step excess 1e-14, float rounding). At the default sliders (0.6/0.1/0.9) and at any setting with alpha+beta <= decay the scale is exactly 1, so those trajectories are bit-identical to before (router.ts 5 -> 2.657205 in 6 steps, unchanged).

apps.title: Boids in their own wake
apps.description: Flocking boids coordinate through a shared, decaying velocity grid as well as their neighbour rules; each is pushed by what the other boids wrote into its cell. The V-shapes you may see are not caused by the wakes.

changes: separation divide-by-zero guard (issue #36): in the Boid Update loop the separation branch `if (d < 25) { steerS.x -= dx/d; steerS.y -= dy/d; }` divided by d with no d>0 check, so two boids at exactly the same position produced 0/0 = NaN and that boid left the flock permanently (reproduced on the real page by placing boids[1] on boids[0]: NaN after 1 frame). The condition is now `if (d < 25 && d > 1e-6)`: a pair closer than 1e-6 px (in practice, an exactly coincident pair) contributes no separation term, because the direction between them is undefined. That is the only changed line. The wrap already offsets by width/height here, so it is left untouched. Pairs with d > 1e-6 are unaffected, so any run that never hits a coincidence is bit-identical to before.

Own-wake leak removed (v1.1, triage 2026-09-24 / review boid_drafting M2): each boid read its grid cell (the 'draft' push) before writing its own velocity into the same persistent cell, so it was pushed by its own earlier deposits: a lone boid started at speed 0.5 reached the 3.5 cap (seeds 1-3, 200 steps, wake push 1.5 and 3; flat 0.5 at push 0). The grid is now stored as flat Float32Arrays, and alongside the total each boid's own share is kept, written with exactly the amount it added (after the existing +-2 clamp) and spread/faded by the same 3x3 mean and (1-diss). A boid is pushed by total minus its own share. Lone-boid probe on the fix: 0.5 / 0.5 / 0.5 at push 0 / 1.5 / 3 (seeds 1-3). Positive control: a boid 100 px behind a leader at speed 3 still gains speed from the leader's wake (0.50 -> 0.528 in 40 steps, seed 1). The blur is done as two 1-D passes over the same in-grid-neighbour mean, identical to the old 3x3 box result. Rendering still shows the total.

Minimum-image neighbours (v1.1): positions wrap but neighbour offsets did not, so boids on opposite edges ignored each other and cohesion pulled across the whole screen. dx, dy are now taken the shortest way across the edges, and cohesion steers toward the mean offset (centroid in the wrapped frame).

Text (v1.1): description rewritten per wording.md 3.7 and triage (no 'drafting', 'reactive fluid grid', 'echelon and V-formations'); labels Wake fade per step / Wake push strength / Stay close / Keep apart; embedded cogdoc block added. Measured: heading agreement |mean unit heading| after 1500 steps, seeds 1-9, fix: push 0 mean 0.85, push 1.5 mean 0.77 (wide spread, 0.47-0.99 and 0.59-1.0), so the claim that the wakes line the flock up is not made.
version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: behaviour change (own-wake leak, periodic neighbours) plus text.

apps.title: Boid Vector Field Simulator
apps.description: Agents navigate a dynamic flow field generated via continuous noise, experiencing advection and rheotaxis.

changes: separation divide-by-zero guard (issue #36): in the Flocking loop the separation branch `if (d < 20) { steerS.x -= dx/d; steerS.y -= dy/d; }` divided by d with no d>0 check, so two boids at exactly the same position (made likely by the wrap, which snaps a boid onto the opposite edge with `b.x = 0` / `b.x = width` rather than offsetting it) produced 0/0 = NaN, and that boid's position went NaN and silently left the flock for good (reproduced on the real page: seed 1, 2500 frames, flowStrength 0, 1 of 150 boids NaN). The condition is now `if (d < 20 && d > 1e-6)`: a pair closer than 1e-6 px (in practice, an exactly coincident pair) contributes no separation term, because the direction between them is undefined. That is the only changed line. The wrap is deliberately left as it was, since the guard alone removes the NaN and changing the wrap would alter every default trajectory. Pairs with d > 1e-6 are unaffected, so any run that never hits a coincidence is bit-identical to before.

apps.title: Slime-mould trails
apps.description: Dots lay scent on a wrap-around grid that spreads and fades, sniff three spots ahead and turn toward the strongest; with no other contact they gather into trail structures (a modified Jones 2010 Physarum model).

changes: head, after <title>: added an embedded <script type="application/cogdoc+yaml"> frontmatter block carrying the canonical cogdoc fields (id/type/title/sector/status/created/authors/tags) plus paper-specific claim, method[] (every slider declared with range, default, unit and meaning), observables, findings, limitations, and typed refs[]. Inert to the renderer (scripts of unknown type are not executed and do not display), so the file is simultaneously an indexable cogdoc of type `paper` and a running artifact — the .cog.html convention. Type `paper` is value 4 of the canonical 19-type enum in .cog/conf/spec/canonical-cogdoc-frontmatter-schema.cog.md and required `id` because it is a sequenced type.

reset()/imageData lifetime fix: the original called `const imageData = ctx.createImageData(width, height)` ONCE at top level immediately after the first reset(). Two failures followed. (1) A container reporting zero width at first layout made createImageData throw IndexSizeError, and because the throw was top-level the subsequent `animate()` call never ran — the simulation was permanently dead on that load, not merely unseeded; the resize listener then re-ran reset() successfully, so the canvas sized correctly and still nothing drew. (2) On any resize, reset() reallocated `grid`/`nextGrid` to the new dimensions while `imageData` retained the old ones, so the render loop wrote into a buffer of the wrong size. Fixed by declaring `let imageData` and reallocating it inside reset() alongside the grid, and by flooring both dimensions with Math.max(64, ...) so a zero-width parent cannot throw at all. This is the same repair welded_fields already carried at lines 249-265, whose comment 'reallocated with the grid, unlike the original' names this exact defect; the correction is now applied to the original rather than only annotated beside it. Verified in-browser after the fix: canvas 490x316, 25793 lit pixels, animation running, zero console errors.
version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: additive frontmatter plus a behavioral bug fix, no change to the model, its parameters, or its visual output.

Periodic boundary (v1.2, triage 2026-09-24 / review physarum E5): the edge rule was 'wrap position AND heading += pi', which is neither a torus nor a reflection: a dot crossing an edge was sent straight back across it and shuttled on the seam forever (single-dot trace on main: x 0.63 -> 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 599 at frames 3/6/9/12/40, heading +pi each crossing). The blur also skipped out-of-grid neighbours while still dividing by 9 and sensors past an edge read 0, so the field was absorbing while positions wrapped. Now all three wrap: position (no heading change), the 3x3 blur (neighbours taken modulo width/height) and sensing (sample coordinates modulo width/height). Measured with the page's own script in a node harness (seeded Math.random identical to real_page_probe.py; reproduces the review's E1 masses 951k/757k/592k exactly), fraction of dots within 1 cell of an edge after 3000 steps, 600x400 grid, uniform random start, seeds 1-3: main 8.2% / 18.2% / 37.9% -> fix 0.83% / 0.30% / 0.29% (even spread = 0.83%). Keep-rate-0 control, 1500 steps, seeds 1-3: 74.4% / 75.1% / 74.5% -> 0.75% / 0.71% / 0.64%. Single-dot trace on the fix: crosses at frame ~4 and keeps heading 3.442 (x 597.8, 594.9, 592.0, 565.3). Real-page confirmation: see PR body.

Density and spawn (v1.2): N was a fixed 8000 while the grid follows the window, so density depended on window size, and the spawn disk radius width/4 overflowed on wide windows (1500x312 grid: 2602 of 8000 dots spawned outside the grid). Now N = max(500, round(width*height/30)) (exactly 8000 at the default 600x400 grid) and spawn radius = min(width, height)/4 (0 out of bounds at 1500x312). At the default size the radius drops from 150 to 100 cells; ring-start outcome at 3000 steps, seeds 1-3, fix with radius 150 vs 100: 50% of dots in 0.21/0.37/0.21% vs 0.21/0.19/0.27% of 8-px bins, 0 dots near an edge in both. Not a material change.

Embedded cogdoc and UI text rewritten (v1.2): finding C4 'ties go to the incumbent' contradicted the code (forward is kept only when strictly greater than both flanks; a forward==flank tie turns to the flank); the text now states the rule as coded, and the rule is unchanged. Finding C5 'SATURATION IS REACHABLE AND DESTROYS COORDINATION' rested on an equilibrium that ignored clamp loss and was withdrawn; replaced by the measured statement that the 255 cap truncates deposit (about 97% of each step's deposit clipped at the defaults, seeds 1-3) and caps contrast, while 0% of dots saw three equal samples. Jones (2010) cited as implements-modified with the deviations (no occupancy exclusion, deposit 25 with a cap, no random order) in limitations; 'global structure' replaced by 'trail structures' plus the controls that remove them. Labels per wording.md 3.7 (Sniff angle / Turn angle / Scent kept per step / Start over, title 'Slime-mould trails').
version 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0: behaviour change (periodic boundary, area-scaled N, fitted spawn disk) plus text corrections.

apps.title: Welded Asteroids
apps.description: The closed-loop stigmergic field itself, living on the quotient surfaces of the topology game: physarum agents, trail and agent-deposited momentum all obey the surface's gluing rule. Six tour levels bind surface + parameter presets + a beta_1 target; 18 declared sliders drive the physarum; the asteroids game survives as a hidden Easter egg (X when beta_1 >= 42). v2.0.1: seam crossings now transform position AND heading together (topo-asteroids flipP protocol — fixes agents stranding at the Klein/projective seams); sim square letterboxed to true 1:1 (fixes stretched height map). v2.1.0: the real fix for the Klein seam-wall — three compounding defects. (1) foldRead/momRead/uvOf mirrored the WRONG axis (topo.y.flip='x' names the axis that mirrors; the code mirrored the other one), so agent sensing disagreed with deposits. (2) Diffusion sampled neighbors with plain torus wrap; on a mirrored identification the flux at the seam never cancels and mass was slowly pumped into the two seam rows — the minutes-scale accumulator. Now neighbor sampling honors the gluing rule (mirrored cell across a mirrored seam) for trail AND momentum, with the vector's mirrored component sign-flipping. (3) Sense samples crossing a mirrored seam have swapped left/right meaning relative to the agent's square frame; the turn rule now swaps L/R when the front and a flank read different fold images — near-seam agents no longer turn back into the seam. Also fixed: wrapPos wrap-count for negative coordinates (floor division) and double-flip when a y-fold pushed x out of range. Verified: 150s Klein soak — no seam wall, no edge pinning; torus/projective/Mobius 45s soaks all stable. v2.2.0: the height map projects the topology — 3D vertices displace along their base normal by the folded trail height (ridges = built loops, valleys = evaporated field), texture texels fold so the parametrization shows the true pullback at every seam, contour lines and agent points ride the same displaced surface, and a '3D relief' slider (0..1) controls the amplitude. Lit MeshStandardMaterial with key/rim lights so relief reads as form. v2.3.0: color separation + seam-continuous contours. Chemical field stays green; contour overlays recolored to the violet family; agents drawn as cyan-white dots (2D overlay + 3D points) so they read against the chemical; wireframe seam guides dimmed violet. Contour segments touching a canvas edge are redrawn shifted by the wrap so closed loops read continuously across the weld instead of chopping off. v2.3.1: operator-reported 3D misalignment (left planes not lining up) — root cause: the v2.2.0 texture/relief path folded the uv a second time (guessing the parametrization needed the sim's mirror), but the surface parametrization already IS the folded immersion; the extra fold split the texture along a line the geometry never folds. foldUv is now the identity — the gluing lives in the parametrization and the sim-side foldRead, exactly once each. v2.3.2: Codex co-review (gpt-6-astra, read-only) confirmed the operator's residual 3D misalignment was a VERTICAL TEXTURE FLIP — three.js CanvasTexture defaults flipY=true, so texture rows ran opposite to the height sampling rows. Fixed with flipY=false. Two follow-on defects from the same review: entities (contours, agent points) now ride the ACTUAL displaced mesh via barycentric interpolation instead of the analytic surface (they floated/sank between mesh vertices), and relief 0 now restores base positions instead of freezing the last displacement. v2.3.3: hardened the overlay against a devicePixelRatio desync — the canvas is sized and transformed with the DPR live at fit time, but the draw paths re-read devicePixelRatio, and a window dragged to a display of different pixel density changes it without firing resize. Scale is now committed once per fit (ovSX/ovSY), a matchMedia (resolution: Ndppx) listener refits on density change, and a ResizeObserver on the sim panel covers layout changes that never resize the window. NOTE: this was a real latent defect but NOT the cause of the operator's report — see v2.3.4. v2.3.4: the actual cause of the operator-reported quarter-size overlay — drawContours computed the grid→CSS scale and then never applied it. buildContour emits paths in GRID units (0..W) because segStore is reused for the 3D push, so the strokes must carry the scale themselves; without it contours drew one grid unit per CSS pixel, filling a W-sized patch in the top-left of an s-sized box. The error is W/s, so it is invisible when the sim panel is about W wide and grows with the window — which is why it read as 'quarter size' on a wide window and looked fine on a narrow one. Strokes now run under octx.scale(sx,sy) with line widths divided back out so the authored weights hold; segStore stays in grid units for the 3D push. The test port exposes __welded.ovScale so the registration can be measured rather than eyeballed. Verified at a 1355x760 viewport: violet contour centroid (0.711, 0.518) against field centroid (0.716, 0.527) on the sim canvas — agreement to within 0.01 of the canvas, where the pre-fix overlay centroid sat at (0.336, 0.334) against a field centroid of (0.500, 0.498). v2.4.0: the 3D shell is now a declared render mode — translucent (new default), wireframe, or solid. A closed quotient surface occludes its own far side, so the opaque shell hid exactly what the panel exists to show: the loops, contours and agents on the back of the torus, and the figure-8 Klein's pass-through entirely. The lever is depthWrite, not opacity — a transparent shell that still writes depth hides everything behind it however see-through it looks; translucent and wireframe both drop depthWrite so the whole shape reads at once. The mode is reapplied on every surface rebuild and is drivable from the test port via __welded.setShell(), with state().shell reporting it. v2.5.0: the sim became runnable as an experiment rather than only watchable. The physics was inside the rAF callback, so it advanced only while the page was painted — a hidden tab froze it and a run's length was wall-clock, not step count. simStep() is now the unit of time and loop() is one simStep plus one paint. Every stochastic draw goes through a seeded stream (mulberry32), spawn can be 'disc' (the ancestor's, still the interactive default) or 'uniform', and the test port gains pause/resume/step(n) plus run(spec) — {seed, surface, spawn, params, at:{step:{...}}, steps} — which returns a manifest that replays identically. PARAMETERS ARE PINNED TO THE TIMELINE: a change is declared at a step index, fires exactly once there, is recorded in the manifest, and drives the slider so the panel cannot show 60 degrees while the sim runs at 90. A run mutated by hand mid-flight is not reproducible, which is how a reported state became unrecoverable. Verified: identical seed reproduces the grid bit-for-bit, a different seed does not, a scheduled change alters the outcome and still replays, and stepping runs at full CPU with the page hidden. v2.5.1: three code paths disagreed about which axis a mirrored weld flips. topo.<axis>.flip NAMES the mirroring axis — Klein is y:{flip:'x'}, so crossing the y-seam mirrors x. wrapPos (agent re-entry) and diffuseDecay's nbT (trail diffusion) read it that way; foldRead mirrored the CROSSED axis instead, so an agent sensing past the weld read the field from a point its own deposits never reach, and momRead flipped vx — per its own comment, which states the correct rule — while folding the coordinate in y. Verified at (40, H+10) on the Klein: re-entry (260,10) and diffusion (259,10) against sensing (40,289). foldRead now honours the named axis; __welded.ablate({seamFold:'legacy'}) reproduces the old path as a control. MEASURED AND NEGATIVE: this does NOT remove the Klein seam accumulation. Uniform spawn, seeds 11 and 22, 4000 steps, both arms end at 11-12.5x the uniform expectation for the rows either side of the weld, against 0.0-0.3 on the torus control. The inconsistency was real; it is not the cause of the accumulation, which remains unexplained and may be genuine dynamics — a mirror line is a natural condensation locus for a physarum network. v2.6.0: slice scope — a planar section of the torus at height c cuts the surface in two circles; the trail is sampled on both and their per-theta difference is normalized by the clamped dimensional radius rho_c = R + sqrt(max(0, r^2 - c^2)), the section's actual radial reach. The diff profile encodes the plane the physarum structure lives on: flat ~0 means toroidally uniform, +mean is an outer-wall (equator-like) loop, -mean a bore (polar) loop, and a sinusoidal diff is a tilted/Villarceau-like band whose first-Fourier phase reveals the plane's orientation and whose amplitude the off-plane share. Panel: z slider, hi/lo/diff strip chart, live rho_c, Delta-bar/rho_c, amp and phase readouts; also exposed on the test port as __welded.slice(). v2.7.0: quadrant scope + gyroscopic readout — two orthogonal planes through the torus axis carve the ring into four quarter-sections whose trail masses are live (the 'clean quarter slice'). The torus provides the reference frame: the field's center of mass is computed every frame directly from the grid, mapped through the embedding to xyz, and reported in toroidal coordinates — rho (radial offset from the central ring), z, and omega, the per-step precession rate of the COM about the axis (frame-to-frame theta difference). The quadrant panel shows the ring from above with cutting planes, quarter-mass arc thickness, the COM marker displaced by rho, and a 120-step precession trace. Balanced ring = COM on axis, omega ~ 0; a tilted off-axis structure shows a nonzero rho with a precessing theta — the gyroscopic reading. On the test port: __welded.com(), __welded.quadrants(). v2.8.0: collector plates — the four quarter-sections reframed as accelerator pickup electrodes (beam-position monitor): the readout is the normalized difference b = (b_x, b_y) = ((Q_R - Q_L)/(sum), (Q_U - Q_D)/(sum)) in [-1,1]^2, which divides out total trail intensity entirely. |b| is how off-axis the field's mass sits, atan2(b_y, b_x) is the steering angle (the precession angle in BPM dress), and the trace of (b_x, b_y) over time is the precession plot — total-charge-free and comparable across runs. The panel shows the four plates at the rim brightening by collected charge, the steering vector on a crosshair, and a 180-step trace. Balanced beam reads (0,0) at any brightness; a beam hugging one plate reads toward +-1. On the test port: __welded.plates(). v2.9.0: mobile/fold experience — the 3D pane takes touch-action:none so one-finger drag orbits instead of scrolling the page, plus two-pointer pinch zoom (distance delta drives camera distance, pointer capture per pointer, cancel-safe). On narrow or coarse-pointer screens the three fixed panels (sidebar | sim | 3D) become a stacked tabbed stage: a two-tab bar (sim / 3D) switches which pane is full-width, and the control sidebar becomes a slide-in drawer behind a fixed hamburger toggle. Desktop layout untouched (media query only). v2.10.0: Villarceau scope — the third slice family as an instrument. A plane tilted alpha from the equator cuts the torus in a loop pair whose topology flips at the critical angle sin(alpha*) = r/R (26.74 deg on the sim's R=1, r=0.45 embedding): separate pair below, exact tangent (Villarceau, linked circles) at, interlaced pair above. The scope solves the section condition per tube angle (n-hat . torusXYZ(u,v) = d is linear in cos u, sin u -> 0/1/2 roots), samples the trail on both branch curves, and reads per-v traces plus first-harmonic amp/phase and a loop-correlation 'link' scalar that climbs toward 1 as the loops merge (measured: 0 at alpha=0, 0.89 at alpha=85). The obliquity dial is free 0-90 deg with the critical angle and live regime (separate/tangent/interlaced) labeled on the panel — the obliquity of the slicing plane is itself a probe coordinate, completing the multidimensional-oscilloscope chart alongside the equatorial slice scope and the axial quadrant scope. Design doc: docs/villarceau-scope.md. Verified headless: regime classification flips exactly at alpha*, 0 page errors, port __welded.vill()/VLS. v2.10.1: Villarceau scope solver correction + honest readouts (post adversarial review: GPT-6 Astra via Codex, plus an earlier independent review; both instrument records preserved). HIGH: villSection solved the wrong equation — the plane condition A(v)cos u + B(v) = d has B constant in u (z-term), but v2.10.0 treated it as a sin-u coefficient (atan2/acos phase-shift form) and sampled near-misses of the true plane (residual up to ~0.7 tube radii). Correct roots u = ±arccos((d-B)/A); sampled points now satisfy the plane condition to 1e-15. HIGH: alpha=0 degeneracy — the centered section reduces to the equatorial pair; villSample(alpha=0) now delegates to sliceSample(c=0), passing the design doc's agreement test that v2.10.0 failed (mean diff 2 vs 0 on a synthetic field). SEMANTICS: same-plane tangent section circles CROSS TRANSVERSELY (53.49 deg on this torus) — 'tangent' is plane-torus contact, not circle-circle tangency; same-plane sections are coplanar so linking number is 0/undefined; the linked Villarceau pair is same-handed circles from DIFFERENT rotated critical planes (verified Gauss linking -1 at 60 deg azimuth). 'link' readout relabeled 'agree' (uncentered cosine similarity — not Pearson, not linkage; scene-dependent); added 'sep' = minimum 3D separation between branch curves. Dial snaps to alpha* within +-0.5 deg; regime labels separate/near-alpha*/separated; stats computed over valid samples only; plot scale no longer mixes angle column into amplitude; readout split into three short lines that fit the canvas; dead VREC/VLS.trans removed; design doc revised (docs/villarceau-scope.md v2). Core theorem sin(alpha*) = r/R survives both reviews; alpha* = 26.744 deg on the sim torus. v2.11.0: external confinement field + energy ledger (docs/confinement-field.md). Tokamak analog: field lines are exact slopes dv/du=q on the quotient chart — the safety factor as geometry. Three knobs: winding q, coupling kappa, cross-field drift nu; three modes: closed (byte-identical v2.10.1 behavior), field-on (open system, P_in billed), field-decaying (single-run tau_sim shutoff protocol). Energy ledger: P_in = kappa*40/q (injection), P_loss = trail evaporation + drift leakage, W_stored = coherent trail mass + momentum coherence, tau_sim = W/P_in. q-histogram: per-agent winding number peaks at the driving rational under strong coupling — VERIFIED: locks at 2.02 for q=2, coherence 0.99 (rational-surface resonance analog, the prediction from the tokamak mapping thread). Bootstrap window (stigmergic substitution for external confinement) instrumented via kappa-reduction protocol; result pending experiment. v2.11.0-rc bug caught in verification: confDir returned slope q^2 (1/q,q); fixed to (1,q) → q locked correctly. v2.11.1: q-histogram instrument correction. v2.11.0 accumulated HEADING vectors (cos a, sin a) with a decay — agents parked on the field direction have the front/back degeneracy (a and a+pi give the same tan) and the decay drove the winding-number distribution onto a fixed attractor (~1.8) DECOUPLED from the driving q; the rational-lock verification of v2.11.0 was this bug reading as a lock (q-peak read 2.02 at every q). Fixed: accumulate wrap-aware chart-position deltas — the path's TRUE winding number q_agent = dv/du. Verified: q-peak now tracks driving q monotonically (q=1 -> 1.02, 1.5 -> 1.27, 2 -> 1.68, 2.5 -> 2.02, 3 -> 2.48, all at coherence 1.000). Residual ~0.83x under-read at high q is real cross-field displacement (momentum advection + drift), not instrument error — 'effective q vs nominal q' is now a measurable quantity. Also: v2.11.0 sweep finding recorded — P_loss under-bills drift by ~2 orders (parts x nu vs evaporation-dominated loss); tau_sim is drift-insensitive; ledger loss model needs actual cross-field heading error (queued v2.11.2). v2.11.2: no-bugs-stand pass (internal audit + adversarial review, Astra usage-limited mid-run; its finding folded in). CRITICAL: field-decaying mode was dead — P_in multiplied by CF.decay=0 snapped to 0 AND full coupling kept steering (free field); now P_in decays (shutdecay=0.97) and coupling decays with it (effKappa = kappa * sqrt(P_in/P_in0)) — the shutoff protocol actually measures confinement decay. HIGH: confinement field was not globally well-defined on mirrored surfaces (Klein/projective/Mobius): uniform slope-q maps to slope -q under the seam flip — confDir now transforms through flipV per seam image (position-dependent via the fold); q-histogram deltas likewise flip-transformed across mirrored seams. HIGH: W_stored momentum term was raw magnitude (scaled with intensity, mislabeled coherence) — now true alignment fraction in [0,1]. MEDIUM: P_loss under-billed drift ~2 orders (billed the dial value) — now bills actual cross-field heading error mean|sin(field-heading)| per agent. MEDIUM: qAccum/qPrev stale after resetField (ghost deltas) — cleared on reseed. LOW: dead code removed (confApply stub, lastW); field-arrows checkbox now draws a real seam-aware arrow overlay (CF.arrows). Verified: shutoff P_in monotonically decays 18->14.99 over 7s, tau finite through decay, structure retention 1.077 (field decayed, structure held — first bootstrap-flavored signal, pending proper experiment); Klein coherence 0.998 with seam-aware field; 0 page errors. v2.11.3: Opus-review fix pass. Ledger computes in ALL modes (closed-mode early return blinded the shutoff experiment). W_stored = trail CONTRAST (excess mass above uniform mean), not trail mass — the old metric saturated at ~175k for fog and field alike; the cold-closed control matched the field-on steady state exactly, killing the v2.11.2 'bootstrap signature' claim (measurement refutation, not physics). Cross-field error/leak only computed against an ACTIVE field (phantom-field artifact removed: cf read 0.65 in closed mode against a field that wasn't there) and scales with applied coupling in decaying mode. Momentum term = true alignment order parameter |sum mom|/sum|mom| (old mean-magnitude was a density proxy latched at 1). tauSim only defined at constant P_in (field-on); decaying-mode tau must come from structure-decay fits (b1/slice-FWHM), not a vanishing denominator. P_in0 decay reference seeded before first decay step (off-by-one). Drift is a true CROSS-FIELD kick (perpendicular to field lines), not isotropic jitter. VERDICT from the fixed instrumentation: post-shutoff W rise (90k->138k) matches the cold-closed control (92k->145k) at identical saturated coverage — the W/contrast metric cannot distinguish structure from diffusion transient; bootstrap remains UNPROVEN. Discriminating instruments for the next pass (Opus-specified): beta-1 persistence, slice-FWHM, quadrant-omega lock, and a new internal-coherence readout (heading vs trail-momentum, not vs the external field). v2.11.5:  v2.11.5: Pauli-exclusion analog for the agents (occupancy blockade, per the crowding-control precedent from boid_drafting). Two dials: exclR (occupancy radius in cells, 0=off) and exclK (stiffness 0-1: soft = heading-coincidence-weighted steering away from occupied cells via the seam-aware momentum field; >=0.75 hard = veto of the chosen move onto an occupied cell with stochastic second-choice fallback and pin counting). Occupancy is LAGGED (built from previous-frame positions on the BASE image via foldRead — mirror images are the same physical place on the quotient) and order-invariant; gated so exclR=0 is bit-identical to v2.11.4. Pressure readout exclReject (rejections/step) + pin rate in the manifest. Motivation: exclusion adds the fermionic half of the phase diagram (degeneracy pressure; band-filling); connects to twistronics flat-band regime (interaction-dominated when kinetic quenched). MEASURED v2.11.5 (post-review, with controls): exclR=0 bit-identical to v2.11.4 after all fixes (checksum 17500000.02153451). C1 self-repulsion bug found by Claude Code review, fixed (lone-agent step length flat 1.012 across exclK 0-0.7; pre-fix it rose to 1.79). Counters reset per run + dedicated rndExcl stream (arms share physarum noise); foldRead negative-coordinate mirror fixed; occTmp removed; jitter ablation control added (exclMode). Final sweep (seed 77, N=7000, 4000 steps, kappa 0/0.3/0.8, arms: control / excl-soft K=0.5 / jitter / excl-hard K=0.9): (1) kappa=0.8 user regime — control b1 collapses 21->0 by 2500 steps; exclusion and jitter arms both keep b1 alive (2-8) through 4000 steps — structure preservation is REAL but perturbation-strength-mediated, NOT exclusion-specific (jitter control matches). (2) kappa=0.3 — the finding: soft exclusion CRYSTALLIZES the swarm into ~11 parallel slope-1 lines (perpendicular rms 6.4 cells vs 81.8 control; jitter control only narrows to 43.8) — a genuine filled-ladder/1D-crystal state, exclusion-specific, OPPOSITE sign to the widen prediction. The old filled-shell refutation is RETRACTED: at moderate coupling exclusion produces band-filling after all, as parallel copies of the band rather than a wider band. (3) q-lock survives all arms (q 0.95-1.0, coherence 0.94-1.0). Documented caveats: hard mode is a lagged blockade (same-frame double occupancy possible); soft kick up to 1.9 cells/step can overshoot the stencil; heading-coincidence clause is coarse (momentum lattice MS=8 vs stencil R<=3) — soft exclusion acts as density repulsion except at momentum-block boundaries. v2.11.6: version badge (top-left, sim+3D); 3D auto-spin removed — orbit fully drag-controlled. v2.11.7: fix — #verBadge CSS rule lost in the v2.11.6 rebase (badge div rendered unpositioned/invisible); rule restored. v2.11.8 (#39): the Möbius strip's walls now hold for the field as well as the agents. Agents REFLECT off the free edges (y and heading mirrored; they were clamped, which pinned 52-88% of the population on the two wall rows after 2500 steps). Trail and momentum diffuse with no-flux edges and every read past an edge sees the edge row: before, nb/nbT, foldRead and momRead wrapped y periodically, so the Möbius field actually lived on a Klein bottle. The Möbius edge word is corrected from 'a b a⁻¹ c' (a cylinder's) to 'a b a c'. tau_sim = W_stored / P_loss (it divided by P_in, the dial constant 40κ/q). The unused 'coherent' sum in the ledger is removed.

changes: head, after <title>: added an embedded <script type="application/cogdoc+yaml"> frontmatter block carrying the canonical cogdoc core (id `paper-welded-fields`, type `paper`, title, description, sector, status, created, updated, salience, authors, tags) plus the paper-conditional fields required by .cog/conf/spec/cogdoc-html-executable-artifacts.cog.md: `claim`, `method[]` with one entry per free parameter (all 18 sidebar sliders plus fixed N=9000, each with range, default, unit where applicable, and a MEANING — a parameter with no stated meaning is a knob, not a method), `observables` naming window.__sim and the cost of each call, `findings[]`, `limitations[]`, and typed `refs[]`. WHY: the artifact previously asserted its corrections in code comments only — line 265's 'reallocated with the grid, unlike the original' and line 625's coverage-vs-level note were unaddressable and uncountable. Spec rule 5 requires any 'unlike the original'-class comment to become a typed ref, so the physarum correction is now `refs[] uri:app:physarum rel:corrects` and is queryable as a graph edge rather than folklore. Spec rule 4 requires an artifact that makes a claim to expose and NAME a test port; window.__sim already existed (commented 'exposed for verification from the console') but was undeclared, so `observables` now names it and cogdoc_verify.py exercises it. The block is inert to the renderer (scripts of unknown type are neither executed nor rendered), so the file is simultaneously a running artifact and an indexable cogdoc. Type `paper` is value 4 of the canonical 19-type enum and is a sequenced type, hence the required `id`.

version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: additive frontmatter only. No change to the model, its parameters, its defaults, or its rendered output — the sole edit is the inert <script> block in <head>. Declared here because this app is kind `frozen-golden` and spec rule 3 makes any edit to a frozen-golden entry a declared change with its reason. Verified after the edit: cogdoc_html.py validate -> OK [paper] paper-welded-fields with zero errors and zero warnings; headless Chromium load via cogdoc_verify.py -> canvas non-zero, lit pixels non-zero, zero console errors, and __sim.betti()/refs() checked against the stated findings.

topology census made periodic (issue #38). euler() and components() (the `topology` block before measure()) read the mask as a zero-padded flat square (bit-quads over x,y in [-1,W) x [-1,H) with out-of-range cells = 0; flood fill skipped out-of-range neighbours) while the agents, trail diffusion and momentum field all wrap on a torus. Fixed: bit-quads now run over x,y in [0,W) x [0,H) with indices taken mod W,H, the 8-neighbour flood fill wraps mod W,H, and measure() and __sim.betti() use the torus relation chi = b0 - b1 + b2, i.e. b1 = b0 + b2 - euler() with b2 = 1 only when the mask covers every cell. Cogdoc observables.betti, limitations[0] and the panel note restated to match; no dynamics, parameter or default changed. Verified by driving analytic masks through the page's own measure() on the real page (605x400; torus answer / before / after, as b0,b1): empty 0,0 / 0,0 / 0,0; disk in the interior 1,0 / 1,0 / 1,0; disk centred on the corner seam 1,0 / 4,0 / 1,0; full-width band 1,1 / 1,0 / 1,1; ring crossing the x-seam 1,1 / 2,0 / 1,1; full-width + full-height cross 1,2 / 1,0 / 1,2; full mask 1,2 / 1,0 / 1,2. EFFECT ON THE HEADLINE OBSERVABLE, stated plainly: at the defaults (thr = 8% coverage) the census read the same before and after on all 5 seeds tested at 1500 frames (seeded run, before (b0,b1) = after (b0,b1) = s1 2,1; s2 2,0; s3 1,2; s4 3,0; s5 2,1) and at 2400 frames, because the swarm is seeded in a central disk and at 8% coverage the mask had no cell pair across the seam in any of those runs. The flat census only diverges once the mask touches the seam: at 20% and 40% coverage after 2400 frames, seed 1 (82 seam pairs) and seed 5 (26 seam pairs) read b0 = 2 flat vs 1 on the torus (b1 unchanged in those cases). So the paper's coverage-invariance finding is not overturned by this fix at its defaults, but b1 values measured earlier at high coverage or on long runs were counts on the square, not the torus, and are not comparable with values from this version.
